Curious what everyone is expecting this preseason for the Browns. I know you can't tell too much from preseason but it's nice to see the team on the field after such a long break. I'm really really hoping Manziel just doesn't look lost. I'm still holding out hope for him to be something for us but have no real expectations other than not as bad as last year.

I'm really excited to see how our offensive line shakes out with Erving coming in and Bowie finally healthy. Also pumped to see Duke Johnson in there, anything to push our running game.
Preseason is just over a month away, what are you expecting?

Honestly? Overkill on Manziel talk. I think he'll naturally attract the most amount of attention, though I think that's mostly trivial at this point. Not to minimize our QB plight, but it's not dramatically different from last season.

Personally, I'm more excited about the potential ascendancy of Justin Gilbert combined with the potential of Danny Shelton. If he can get his shit together, we are going to ruin offenses next season on a weekly basis. I personally am going to be looking over every article I can to see how this defense gels this season.
If Gilbert can live up to his potential this season and Shelton is as good as we hope, it's going to be really hard to move the ball against us. Will be very fun tow watch.

I'm mostly curious to see how our DLine looks with everyone back and Shelton in the mix. If we can even be middle of the league in rush defense we will have one of the best defenses in the league. I'm also super curious to see how the WR corps shake out, I'd really like to see Pryor earn a spot on the team as that would say a tremendous amount about his work ethic and athletic ability.

What I think is most important however, is that Manziel looks alright. I want to see that he can handle everything and run the offense while adding in a little of his flair. I'd really like to see him do well in the first 3 games such that he can play 90% of the fourth game. At this point in time I'd rather start the season with McCown unless Manziel shows some serious shit in preseason.

I am not expecting it, but I am really hoping for Pryor to make a splash. Yes, I am a tOSU homer. Yes I want all tOSU players to graduate to the Browns and kickass. Yes, I die a little on the inside when a tOSU player goes to squatsburgh and makes them a better team. Yes, I forgive players for playing at that school up north when they come to Cleveland, but that's totally different. Jeeze, I didn't realize this was going to turn into twenty questions.

Project Almanac is a found footage movie about some highschool kids who build a time machine. And naturally time travely stuff happens but it really isn't that interesting.

I generally don't like the found footage genre in general but I don't hate it either and I'm not docking the movie because of that. As soon as I saw the "mtv productions" logo I knew it wasn't going to be Primer (then again what is). Sadly the MTV influence was prevalent throughout the whole movie including a way-too-long sequence of the crew going back in time to see Lollapalooza.

One part that was realistic: the nerdy guys have a whole series of test planned to make sure its safe for them to use, then the hot chick says (paraphrased) "test are for squares, lets go time travel, tee hee" and the nerdy guys immediately abandon their plans to and do what she says. The aesop of the movie appears to be something like "when the nerdy guy tries to get the hot girl it ends in disaster", but I don't think that is what the filmmakers intended.

I guess I'm too old but I had a hard time identifying or even sympathizing with the characters so I didn't really care what happened to them. That made the experience more tedious than entertaining. There one original idea but not enough to carry the picture.

Should you watch it: nope

After seeing it I asked my friend what he would do if he found a time machine and he said he would go back in time to stop himself from watching this movie.
